chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A man marries a woman, lowers the veil over both of them, and closes the door. Then he divorces her. The woman is asked, 'Did he come to you?' She says, 'He did not come to me.' He is asked, 'Did you go to her?' He says, 'I did not go to her.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Both of them are not believed, and that is because she wants to repel the waiting period (iddah) from herself, and he wants to repel the dower (mahr) from himself. Meaning if they are both suspected (of collusion).'

key_terms.السِّتْر: The veil or curtain separating the couple in the marital chamber
key_terms.الْعِدَّة: The waiting period a woman must observe after divorce or death of husband
key_terms.الْمَهْر: The dower or bridal money given by the husband to the wife
key_terms.مُتَّهَمَيْنِ: Two people who are suspected of collusion or deceit in their testimony

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a husband and wife both claim no intercourse occurred to avoid paying the dower and waiting period?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this narration from Abu Basir highlights the principle of 'tuhmah' (suspicion of collusion) in marital disputes, where the husband and wife conspire to evade the financial burden of the dower (mahr) and the waiting period (iddah). Shia jurists utilize this hadith to establish that when both parties have a vested interest in denying consummation, their testimony is discounted, ensuring the husband pays the full dower and the wife bears the costs of her iddah. This ruling underscores the prophetic emphasis on preventing legal loopholes in family law to protect the rights of both spouses.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The man married the woman, so he loosened (his clothes) upon it, and upon her was a veil, and he locked the door. Then he divorced her. So the woman was asked, ‘Did he come to you?’ So she is saying, ‘He did not come to me’. And he was asked, ‘Did you go to her?’ So he is saying, ‘I did not go to her?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Both of them would not be ratified, and that is because she want to repel the waiting period from herself, and he wants to repel the dower from himself – meaning if they were accused’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Ri’ab from abu Basir who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who marries a woman; then pulls the curtains down upon himself and on her and closes the door; then divorces her and the woman is asked, ‘Did he come to you? She says, ‘No, he did not come to me.’ He then is asked, ‘Did you go to her?’ He says, ‘No, I did go to her.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Their words are not accepted because she wants to avoid waiting period from herself and he wants to avoid mahr (dower), meaning when they are accused.’”
